correctness.rationale: For each selected row or column, three collinear selected vertices are impossible by their unique geodesic. Selected pairwise L1 diameter is at most three. The occupied-row-span dichotomy bounds the size by six. Equality in row span three uniquely forces the 4-by-3 transposed template. Equality in row span two, after excluding a full six-of-nine 3-by-3 square using opposite corner pairs and a three-omission permutation, forces the 3-by-4 template. Six symmetry classes of pairs have explicit free shortest paths. For 3-by-3 grids six is impossible; five is exhibited and a corner/midpoint case analysis shows precisely four maxima. The independent checker lists all 20,675 distance-three cliques on thirteen grids, rechecks original path visibility and complete optimizer sets; its output is included. This finite test supports, not substitutes for, the infinite elementary proof.

originality.rationale: The original 2024-08-07 preprint introducing this invariant explicitly raises exact k-distance mutual visibility of Cartesian path grids as an open research problem. The closest primary results solve other graph families or ordinary unlimited-distance visibility, and none of the inspected stronger/equivalent-formulation results implies the new sharp six-point upper bound or all-optimizer placement counts. Targeted semantic research-record, web, and own-ledger overlap checks found no equivalence; unindexed priority remains possible.
residual_risks: The original 2023 unrestricted Cartesian-product paper was not accessible in complete full text; comparisons use descriptions in accessible later primary articles.
A later or unindexed exact radius-three grid result or equivalent optimization enumeration might exist. The review establishes best-knowledge originality, not bibliographic uniqueness.

value.rationale: This settles a concrete k=3 case of an explicitly posed graph-family open direction, proving an exact constant optimum for arbitrarily large two-dimensional grids, a unique pair of symmetry-related six-point templates, a polynomial exact number of maximal-size selected configurations, and four exceptional 3-by-3 optimizers. The classification of all extremizers is a structural strengthening not supplied by generic lower bounds, not an arbitrary isolated numerical instance.
